title: The upstairs neighbours kept me awake
goal: At university, tell Sēf the neighbours upstairs kept you up all night, and talk through whether to complain
tip: Recycle khalla + person + verb: ma khallūni anām 'they didn't let me sleep', khal il-ḥāris ykallimhum 'get the watchman to talk to them'. Advice is lāzim + verb (lāzim tkallimhum 'you have to talk to them') and idha 'if'. To complain about someone: ashtiki ʿalēhum.
grammar: recycle: khalla + verb (ma khallūni anām), lāzim + verb, idha
dialogue: A
شفيك؟ شكلك تعبان
shfīk? shaklak taʿbān
What's up? You look tired.
B
ما نمت. الجيران اللي فوق ما خلوني أنام
ma nimt. il-jīrān illi fōg ma khallūni anām
I didn't sleep. The upstairs neighbours kept me awake.
A
ما رقدت أبد؟ ليش، شو كانوا يسوون طول الليل؟
ma rgadt abad? lēsh, shu kānaw ysawwūn ṭūl il-lēl?
You didn't sleep at all? Why, what were they doing all night?
B
إزعاج! عيالهم يركضون فوق راسي
izʿāj! ʿyālhum yirkẓūn fōg rāsi
A racket! Their kids run around right over my head.
A
لازم تكلمهم، بس بالراحة. يمكن ما يدرون إن الصوت يوصل لك
lāzim tkallimhum, bas bir-rāḥa. yimkin ma yadrūn inn iṣ-ṣōt yōṣal lak
You have to talk to them, but nicely. Maybe they don't realise the noise reaches you.
B
كلمتهم مرة، وقالوا آسفين. بس ما تغير شي
kallamt-hum marra, w gālaw āsfīn. bas ma tghayyar shay
I talked to them once, and they said sorry. But nothing changed.
A
عيل خل الحارس حق البناية يكلمهم، هذا شغله
ʿayal khal il-ḥāris ḥagg il-bināya ykallimhum, hādha shughlah
Then get the building's watchman to talk to them; that's his job.
B
ما أبي أشتكي عليهم. هم جيراني، وأشوفهم كل يوم
ma abi ashtiki ʿalēhum. hum jīrāni, w ashūfhum kill yōm
I don't want to complain about them. They're my neighbours, and I see them every day.
A
صح كلامك. عيل عطهم أسبوع، وإذا ما تغير شي، خل الحارس يكلمهم
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak. ʿayal ʿaṭhum usbūʿ, w idha ma tghayyar shay, khal il-ḥāris ykallimhum
Fair enough. Then give them a week, and if nothing changes, get the watchman to talk to them.
items: the upstairs neighbours, the neighbours above
the downstairs neighbours: il-jīrān illi taḥt (الجيران اللي تحت)
they didn't let me sleep, they kept me awake
he didn't let me sleep: ma khallāni anām (ما خلاني أنام)
the noise reaches you, you can hear the noise (to a man)
to a woman: iṣ-ṣōt yōṣal lich (الصوت يوصل لج); (recognise)
get the watchman to talk to them (to a man)
to a woman: khalli l-ḥāris ykallimhum (خلي الحارس يكلمهم)
I complain about them, I report them
the watchman, the security guard (of a building)

title: The neighbour at the door
goal: At your flat in Mirdif, the older Emirati neighbour from next door brings food from his family; thank him, offer help, accept his invitation
tip: Offers use idha + past: idha ḥtajt ay shay 'if you need anything' (lit. 'if you needed'). To thank a whole family, put the thanks you know in the group form: ma tgaṣṣrūn, tislam īdkum. To an older man: yā ʿammi; ana ḥāẓir 'I'm at your service', and offer back with w inta baʿad.
grammar: recycle: idha + past for offers (idha ḥtajt), plural you (-kum, -ūn)
dialogue: A
السلام عليكم. أنا جارك، ساكن في الشقة اللي يمك
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. ana jārak, sākin fi sh-shigga illi yammak
Hello. I'm your neighbour; I live in the flat next to yours.
B
وعليكم السلام. حياك الله يا عمي، تفضل
w ʿalaykum is-salām. ḥayyāk allāh yā ʿammi, tfaẓẓal
Hello. Welcome, uncle, come in.
A
الله يحييك. ما بطول، بس الأهل سووا هريس، وقالوا هذا حق الجار
allāh yḥayyīk. ma baṭawwil, bas il-ahal sawwaw harīs, w gālaw hādha ḥagg il-jār
Thank you. I won't stay long; the family made harees and said this is for the neighbour.
B
ما تقصرون والله! تسلم إيدكم
ma tgaṣṣrūn wallāh! tislam īdkum
You're all so kind! Bless your hands.
A
الله يسلمك، ما سوينا شي. وإذا احتجت أي شي، لا تستحي. ترانا الباب بالباب
allāh ysallmak, mā sawwēna shay. w idha ḥtajt ay shay, la tistiḥi. tarāna l-bāb bil-bāb
Not at all, it's nothing. And if you need anything, don't be shy. We're right next door.
B
الله يخليك يا عمي. وانت بعد، إذا تبي شي، أنا حاضر
allāh ykhallīk yā ʿammi. w inta baʿad, idha tabi shay, ana ḥāẓir
Thank you, uncle. And you too: if you want anything, I'm at your service.
A
زين يا ولدي. تعال عندنا يوم الجمعة بعد العصر، نتقهوى ويا عيالي
zēn yā wildi. taʿāl ʿindana yōm il-jumʿa baʿd il-ʿaṣir, nitgahwa wiyya ʿyāli
Good, son. Come over to ours on Friday after the afternoon prayer; we'll have coffee with my sons.
B
إن شاء الله، بيي أكيد
in shāʼ allāh, bayi akīd
God willing, I'll definitely come.
items: (the one) next to you, next door to you (to a man)
to a woman: illi yammich (اللي يمج); yammak is 'beside you', not yumma 'mum'
after the afternoon prayer, in the late afternoon
and you too, the same goes for you (to a man)
to a woman: w inti baʿad (وانتي بعد)
if you need anything (to a man)
to a woman: idha ḥtajti ay shay (إذا احتجتي أي شي)
right next door (lit. door to door)
I'm at your service, I'm ready to help (said by a man)
a woman says: ana ḥāẓra (أنا حاضرة)
we have coffee (together), we'll have coffee
culture: Harees is wheat slow-cooked with meat and ghee until smooth. Cleaning and grinding the grain is hard work, so it is made in big pots: a dish for Ramadan, for guests and for weddings, and one that gets shared. In 2023 it was added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage, nominated by the UAE, Oman and Saudi Arabia.

title: He cut in on me!
goal: Driving on a busy Dubai road with Sēf, complain about other drivers and take his advice to slow down
tip: Recycle w + pronoun + present for 'while': w ana asūg 'while I'm driving', w ana akallim 'while I'm on the phone'. Commands and don'ts: khiff shwayy 'slow down a bit', la tsarriʿ 'don't speed up'. In traffic, dakhal ʿalay is 'he cut in on me'.
grammar: recycle: w + pronoun + present ('while'), commands and la + verb
dialogue: A
شوي شوي يا ريّال! ليش معصب؟
shwayy shwayy yā rayyāl! lēsh mʿaṣṣib?
Easy, man! Why are you so angry?
B
شفت هذا؟ دخل علي فجأة!
shift hādha? dakhal ʿalay fajʼa!
Did you see that? He cut in on me out of nowhere!
A
عادي، في ناس دوم جي. وهذا اللي ورا لاصق فينا ويهرن بعد
ʿādi, fī nās dōm chī. w hādha illi wara lāṣig fīna w yharrin baʿad
That's normal, some people are always like that. And this one behind is right on our tail, honking too.
B
صج! شو يبي هذا؟
ṣij! shu yabi hādha?
Seriously! What does he want?
A
خله يروح. لا تسرع، ترا في رادار هني
khallah yrūḥ. la tsarriʿ, tara fī rādār hni
Let him go. Don't speed up; there's a speed camera here, you know.
B
أنا مب مسرع. بس السواقة هني تعب
ana mub misriʿ. bas is-swāga hni taʿab
I'm not speeding. But driving here is exhausting.
A
أدري. الشهر اللي طاف يتني مخالفة، الكاميرا صورتني وأنا أكلم في التلفون
adri. ish-shahar illi ṭāf yatni mukhālafa, il-kāmira ṣawwaratni w ana akallim fi t-tilifōn
I know. Last month I got a fine: the camera caught me while I was on the phone.
B
عشان جي أنا ما ألمس التلفون وأنا أسوق
ʿashān chī ana ma almis it-tilifōn w ana asūg
That's why I don't touch my phone while I'm driving.
A
زين تسوي. وخف شوي، الشارع كله زحمة
zēn tsawwi. w khiff shwayy, ish-shāriʿ killah zaḥma
Good for you. And slow down a bit; the whole road's jammed.
items: he cut in on me (in traffic); he came in on me
she cut in on me: dakhlat ʿalay (دخلت علي)
right on our tail, (driving) too close behind us
right behind me: lāṣig fīni (لاصق فيني)
slow down a bit, ease off a bit (to a man)
to a woman: khiffi shwayy (خفي شوي)
don't speed up, don't go fast (to a man)
to a woman: la tsarrʿīn (لا تسرعين)
I got a (traffic) fine (lit. a fine came to me)
while I'm driving, while I was driving

title: Metro or car?
goal: At the office, Maryam asks why you still drive to work; weigh up the metro against your car
tip: Recycle comparatives: arīḥ 'more relaxing', awfar 'cheaper'. Concede, then add your but: ṣaḥḥ awfar, bas il-maḥaṭṭa mub garība 'true, it's cheaper, but the station isn't near'. To defend the car: ʿala kēfi 'as I like', wagt ma abi 'whenever I want'.
grammar: recycle: comparatives (arīḥ, awfar), ṣaḥḥ … bas … to concede
dialogue: A
بعدك تيي الدوام بسيارتك؟
baʿdak tiyi d-dawām b-sayyārtak?
Do you still come to work in your car?
B
هيه، بس الزحمة الصبح تعبتني
hē, bas iz-zaḥma ṣ-ṣubḥ taʿʿabatni
Yes, but the morning traffic has worn me out.
A
ليش ما تاخذ المترو؟ أنا آخذه كل يوم، أريح وأوفر
lēsh ma tākhidh il-mitrō? ana ākhdhah kill yōm, arīḥ w awfar
Why don't you take the metro? I take it every day; it's more relaxing and cheaper.
B
صح أوفر، بس المحطة مب قريبة من المكتب
ṣaḥḥ awfar, bas il-maḥaṭṭa mub garība min il-maktab
True, it's cheaper, but the station isn't near the office.
A
عادي، في باص يوصلك. وفي المترو تقدر تقرا أو ترتاح
ʿādi, fī bāṣ ywaṣṣlak. w fi l-mitrō tigdar tigra aw tartāḥ
That's fine, there's a bus that takes you there. And on the metro you can read or relax.
B
بس السيارة على كيفي، أطلع وقت ما أبي
bas is-sayyāra ʿala kēfi, aṭlaʿ wagt ma abi
But with the car I do as I like; I leave whenever I want.
A
والبترول والمواقف؟ حسبتها؟
w il-batrōl w il-mawāgif? ḥasabt-ha?
And the petrol and the parking? Have you worked it out?
B
لا والله ما حسبتها. يمكن أجرب المترو أسبوع
la wallāh ma ḥasabt-ha. yimkin ajarrib il-mitrō usbūʿ
No, honestly, I haven't worked it out. Maybe I'll try the metro for a week.
A
جرب، وقول لي بعدين شو رأيك
jarrib, w gūl-li baʿdēn shu raʼyak
Try it, and tell me afterwards what you think.
items: it's worn me out, it's tired me out (a feminine thing: traffic, work)
(it's) not near the office (a feminine thing: a station, a shop)
a masculine thing: mub garīb (مب قريب)
there's a bus that takes you (there) (to a man)
to a woman: fī bāṣ ywaṣṣlich (في باص يوصلج); (recognise)
do you still come (to)…? (to a man)
to a woman: baʿdich tiyīn…? (بعدج تيين…؟)

title: Weddings cost a fortune now
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, talk about why weddings have got so expensive for young men
tip: Recycle ṣār + verb for 'have started to': ṣārat tkallif wāyid 'they've started costing a lot'. Contrast then and now: ayyām awwal kān … , w il-ḥīn … And the counterfactual lō … chān: lō ana makānhum, chān sawwēt ʿirs ṣghīr.
grammar: recycle: ṣār + verb, ayyām awwal vs il-ḥīn, lō … chān
dialogue: A
الأعراس الحين صارت تكلف وايد، والشباب ما يقدرون عليها
il-aʿrās il-ḥīn ṣārat tkallif wāyid, w ish-shabāb ma yigdarūn ʿalēha
Weddings cost a fortune these days, and young men can't afford them.
B
صح كلامك يا عمي. القاعة والعشا والمعازيم، كل شي غالي
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak yā ʿammi. il-gāʿa w il-ʿasha w il-maʿāzīm, kill shay ghāli
You're right, uncle. The hall, the dinner, the guests: everything's expensive.
A
وفوق هذا المهر. أيام أول كان العرس على قد الحال
w fōg hādha l-mahar. ayyām awwal kān il-ʿirs ʿala gadd il-ḥāl
And on top of that, the mahr. In the old days a wedding was modest.
B
والحين الكل يبي عرس أكبر من غيره
w il-ḥīn il-kill yabi ʿirs akbar min ghērah
And now everyone wants a bigger wedding than the next person.
A
كلام الناس يا ولدي. يخافون شو بيقولون الناس
kalām in-nās yā wildi. ykhāfūn shu biygūlūn in-nās
It's what people will say, son. They're afraid of what people will say.
B
وبعض الشباب يبدون حياتهم وعليهم ديون
w baʿaẓ ish-shabāb yibdūn ḥayāt-hum w ʿalēhum diyūn
And some young men start their married life in debt.
A
هيه، والحكومة تساعدهم بمنحة، بس المفروض ما يبالغون
hē, w il-ḥukūma tsāʿid-hum b-minḥa, bas il-mafrūẓ ma ybālghūn
Yes, and the government helps them with a grant, but they shouldn't go overboard.
B
والله لو أنا مكانهم، جان سويت عرس صغير
wallāh lō ana makānhum, chān sawwēt ʿirs ṣghīr
Honestly, if I were them, I'd have a small wedding.
A
زين قلت يا ولدي. بس نشوف لما تعرس انت!
zēn gilt yā wildi. bas nshūf lamma tʿarris inta!
Well said, son. But we'll see when you get married yourself!
items: they cost a fortune now, they've started costing a lot (plural things)
a masculine thing: ṣār ykallif wāyid (صار يكلف وايد)
they can't afford it, they can't manage it (a feminine thing or plural things)
a masculine thing: ma yigdarūn ʿalēh (ما يقدرون عليه)
the mahr (the groom's marriage gift to the bride)
bigger than the next one, bigger than anyone else's (a masculine thing)
a feminine thing: akbar min ghērha (أكبر من غيرها)
and they're in debt (lit. and debts are on them)
I'm in debt: ʿalay diyūn (علي ديون)
in the old days, back then
culture: The mahr is the groom's marriage gift to the bride, agreed as part of the marriage contract. For Emiratis the law sets an upper limit on it, and the government gives a one-off marriage grant to an Emirati man marrying an Emirati woman, if his income is under a set limit. Even so, many families talk about how hard it has become to keep a wedding simple.
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search «معلم لهجة إماراتية» or «Emirati Arabic tutor»), ask how weddings work in their family: the hall, the guests, the cost. Then give your own view for a minute, using 3 items from this week, e.g. ṣārat tkallif wāyid, kalām in-nās, w ʿalēhum diyūn. Keep it going for 8 turns.

title: National Day plans
goal: Sēf tells you his plans for the UAE's National Day; ask what the day means to him and wish him well
tip: Recycle the future b- for plans: binḥuṭṭ aʿlām 'we'll put flags up', biniṭlaʿ 'we'll go out', bayīb-lak 'I'll bring you'. On a national day the wish is kill ʿām w intu b-khēr 'many happy returns' (lit. every year may you all be well); the reply is w inta b-khēr.
grammar: recycle: future b- for plans (binḥuṭṭ, biniṭlaʿ, bayīb)
dialogue: A
شو بتسوي في اليوم الوطني؟
shu bitsawwi fi l-yōm il-waṭani?
What are you doing for National Day?
B
ما عندي شي. عندنا إجازة يومين، صح؟
ma ʿindi shay. ʿindana ijāza yōmēn, ṣaḥḥ?
Nothing. We get two days off, right?
A
هيه. بنحط أعلام على السيارة، وبنطلع ويا الشباب
hē. binḥuṭṭ aʿlām ʿala s-sayyāra, w biniṭlaʿ wiyya sh-shabāb
Yes. We'll put flags on the car and go out with the guys.
B
حلو! أنا بعد أبي أعلق علم على سيارتي
ḥilu! ana baʿad abi aʿallig ʿalam ʿala sayyārti
Nice! I want to hang a flag on my car too.
A
أكيد! وفي الليل بنشوف الألعاب النارية
akīd! w fi l-lēl binshūf il-alʿāb in-nāriyya
Of course! And at night we'll watch the fireworks.
B
شو يعني لك اليوم الوطني؟
shu yaʿni lak il-yōm il-waṭani?
What does National Day mean to you?
A
هذا عيد الاتحاد يا ريّال، يوم اتحدت الإمارات سنة واحد وسبعين
hādha ʿīd il-ittiḥād yā rayyāl, yōm ittaḥadat il-Imārāt sanat wāḥid w sabʿīn
It's Union Day, man: the day the Emirates united, in '71.
B
ما شاء الله. كل عام وانتو بخير
mā shāʼ allāh. kill ʿām w intu b-khēr
That's wonderful. Many happy returns to you all.
A
وانت بخير! وبييب لك وشاح عشان تلبسه وياي
w inta b-khēr! w bayīb-lak wshāḥ ʿashān tilbasah wiyyāy
And to you! And I'll bring you a scarf so you can wear it with me.
items: (I) hang a flag, put a flag up
what does it mean to you? (to a man)
to a woman: shu yaʿni lich? (شو يعني لج؟)
Union Day (the official name of the UAE's National Day)
many happy returns, happy holiday (lit. every year may you be well) (to a group)
to one man: kill ʿām w inta b-khēr; to one woman: kill ʿām w inti b-khēr; the reply: w inta b-khēr; the plural is usual even to one person (you and yours)
and to you (reply to kill ʿām w inta b-khēr) (to a man)
to a woman: w inti b-khēr (وانتي بخير); to a group: w intu b-khēr (وانتو بخير)
culture: National Day, officially Eid al-Etihad (Union Day), is on 2 December: on that day in 1971 six emirates formed the union, and Ras al-Khaimah joined on 10 February 1972. It is a two-day public holiday, usually around 2 December; the Cabinet sets the dates each year. A month earlier, on 3 November, is Flag Day: at 11 a.m. people across the country raise the flag together.

title: Checkpoint 4.4: Fahad comes for National Day
goal: Checkpoint: Fahad and his cousin visit you in Mirdif over National Day; tell them about your neighbours, plan the evening, and hear about Kuwait's national days
tip: Review, and now you say it: ma khallūna nnām 'they didn't let us sleep', khallhum 'forget them, leave them', maʿak ḥagg, il-khulāṣa, arīḥ and il-ḥilu fīh, kill ʿām w intu b-khēr, and idha ḥtajtu shay 'if you need anything' to a group. Fahad uses Kuwaiti forms (shinu, iḥna).
grammar: checkpoint 4.4 (s4u045–s4u056): khalla + verb, agreeing and pros and cons, comparatives, group forms
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شلونك؟ شكلك ما نمت
hala wallāh! shlōnak? shaklak ma nimt
Hey there! How are you? You look like you haven't slept.
B
هلا فيك! الحمد لله، بس الجيران اللي فوق رجعوا، ما خلونا ننام
hala fīk! il-ḥamdu lillāh, bas il-jīrān illi fōg rijʿaw, ma khallūna nnām
Hey! Fine, thanks, but the upstairs neighbours are at it again; they didn't let us sleep.
A
إحنا بعد عندنا جيران جذي في الكويت. شنو سويتوا؟
iḥna baʿad ʿindana jīrān chidhi fi l-Kwēt. shinu sawwētu?
We've got neighbours like that in Kuwait too. What did you do?
B
كلمنا صاحب الشقة. الخلاصة، خلهم. المهم بنطلع الليلة؟
kallamna ṣāḥib ish-shigga. il-khulāṣa, khallhum. il-muhimm biniṭlaʿ il-lēla?
We talked to the landlord. Bottom line: forget them. The main thing is, are we going out tonight?
A
أكيد! بس الشوارع زحمة، الكل طالع بالأعلام ويهرن
akīd! bas ish-shawāriʿ zaḥma, il-kill ṭāliʿ bil-aʿlām w yharrin
Of course! But the roads are jammed; everyone's out with flags, honking.
B
معك حق. بنروح بالمترو، أريح. الحلو فيه ما في زحمة
maʿak ḥagg. binrūḥ bil-mitrō, arīḥ. il-ḥilu fīh ma fī zaḥma
You're right. We'll take the metro; it's easier. The good thing about it is there's no traffic.
A
زين. وتدري إن عندنا العيد الوطني وعيد التحرير في فبراير؟
zēn. w tadri inn ʿindana l-ʿīd il-waṭani w ʿīd it-taḥrīr fi fibrāyir?
Great. And did you know we have National Day and Liberation Day in February?
B
صج؟ كل عام وانتو بخير من الحين!
ṣij? kill ʿām w intu b-khēr min il-ḥīn!
Really? Many happy returns to you both, in advance!
A
وانت بخير! وتعال الكويت، البيت بيتك، على قد الحال
w inta b-khēr! w taʿāl il-Kwēt, il-bēt bētak, ʿala gadd il-ḥāl
And to you! And come to Kuwait; our home is your home, nothing fancy.
B
إن شاء الله. والحين إذا احتجتوا شي، لا تستحون
in shāʼ allāh. w il-ḥīn idha ḥtajtu shay, la tistiḥūn
God willing. And for now, if you need anything, don't be shy.
culture: Kuwait marks two days in a row. National Day, 25 February, celebrates independence: that was won on 19 June 1961, and since the 1960s it has been celebrated on the anniversary of Sheikh Abdullah Al-Salem taking office. Liberation Day, 26 February, marks the end of the Iraqi occupation in 1991. Both are public holidays.
